sections.overview: The Silver Hook is a small European moth in the noctuid family.
sections.identification: Its olive-brown forewings carry a cream streak and a contrasting spur-shaped mark; the hindwings are usually dusky. The pattern distinguishes it from many other small grass moths, though close inspection is useful.
sections.habitat: It occurs in wet, open habitats, including fens, marshes and boggy heath.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on sedges, especially Carex, and also on coarse grasses such as Deschampsia. These larval food plants are different from the adult moth’s occasional visits to flowers.
sections.behavior: Adults can be disturbed from low vegetation during the day and also come to artificial lights after dusk. In Britain, the flight season is generally reported from late spring into summer.
sections.reproduction: Belgian records report two generations yearly; the species overwinters as a pupa in a cocoon.
sections.ecology: Its distribution is tied to wetland vegetation and the availability of larval sedges and grasses. Because suitable marshes and fens can be local and fragmented, regional records may differ markedly.
sections.conservation: Its assessed status varies geographically: it is listed as Endangered in the Flemish regional assessment but Least Concern in Germany. These regional categories should not be mistaken for a single global assessment.
